basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models the process from authorised need to offer and handoff, not the vacancy, candidate or employment.
Freezes selection criteria before screening so changes can be traced.
Keeps score, recommendation, selection, offer and acceptance as separate assertions.
Includes fairness evaluation and remedies as part of the process.

may: Publish approved postings to sourcing channels.
Schedule interviews and send candidate communications.
Screen applications against frozen criteria and explain each outcome.
Report fairness metrics across process stages.
mustNot: Reject or rank candidates using protected characteristics or proxies for them.
Make a final hiring decision or offer without a human decision maker.
Change criteria after screening started without recording it.
Retain candidate data beyond the stated period or purpose.
Run assessments that the candidate was not told about.
requiresHuman: Any rejection based mainly on automated assessment.
Handling candidate complaints or accommodation requests.

considerations: Hiring decisions shape livelihoods; discrimination by algorithm or proxy must be prevented.
Candidates have rights to information, data protection and reasonable accommodation.
Automated video or psychometric analysis raises dignity and validity concerns.

items: A recruitment process has a requisition, a position, criteria, stages and candidate cases.
It is confused with a job posting, a vacancy, an application or onboarding.
Wrong offers issued from mixed-up candidate records.
